text: Coal power is the single most important thing to switch off to stay in line with 1.5 °C, according to Climate Analytics, the group behind the Climate Action Tracker.
source_name: Climate Analytics: Coal phase-out briefing

text: The world burns more coal than ever. Global coal demand was on course to rise 0.5% in 2025 to a record 8.85 billion tonnes, and China and India account for 71% of it.
source_name: IEA: Coal 2025 (executive summary)

text: The IEA expects demand to slip only about 3% by 2030. That is far short of the cut the UN says is needed.
source_name: Bloomberg Government, reporting IEA Coal 2025

text: For comparison, the UN Environment Programme says coal use must fall 75% by 2035 and be phased out globally by 2040 to return to 1.5 °C after overshoot.
source_name: S&P Global, reporting UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026

text: Put an exit date in law. The Climate Action Tracker's benchmark is coal power gone by 2030 in developed countries and by 2040 in developing ones.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker: Paris-aligned benchmarks for the power sector

text: Stop approving new coal plants. The tracker finds no role for carbon capture on coal power, so fitting it is not a way to keep plants open.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker: power sector briefing

text: Retire plants in a planned order and replace them with renewables, not gas. The same benchmarks also end unabated fossil gas power by 2035 in developed countries and 2040 elsewhere.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker: Pulling the plug on fossils in power

text: Pay for it. Developing countries that rely on coal need international finance to move faster. The tracker calls the Just Energy Transition Partnerships a step in the right direction but not enough.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker: Pulling the plug on fossils in power

text: Plan for coal workers from the start. Research reported alongside IEA data finds most coal workers would struggle to move their skills to other industries, so retraining and regional investment cannot wait until plants close.
source_name: Miningmx, reporting IEA data

text: Governments plan to produce more than double the fossil fuels in 2030 than a 1.5 °C path allows. The gap has widened since the last assessment in 2023.
source_name: Production Gap Report 2025 (SEI, Climate Analytics, IISD)

text: Of the 20 major producing countries reviewed, 17 still plan to increase production of at least one fossil fuel. Together they produce about 80% of the world's fossil fuels.
source_name: Production Gap Report 2025: SEI press release

text: Public money still props the industry up. The fiscal cost of government support for fossil fuels remains near record highs despite repeated pledges to phase out inefficient subsidies.
source_name: Down To Earth, reporting the Production Gap Report 2025

text: At COP30 in Belém, more than 80 countries asked for a roadmap away from fossil fuels. Producers including Russia and Saudi Arabia opposed it, and the final agreement did not mention fossil fuels.
source_name: NPR, COP30 outcome

text: Stop approving new oil and gas fields and new coal mines. The IEA's net zero path needs none beyond what is already approved. In 2025 it repeated this for oil and gas, with some caveats.
source_name: Carbon Brief on the IEA's 2025 finding

text: Plan a managed decline in production. Analysis of the IPCC's 1.5 °C scenarios finds oil and gas output must fall by about 3-4% a year.
source_name: IISD: Zeroing in on finance for oil and gas

text: Make production plans match the country's own climate pledges. Today's plans and projections exceed what the pledges imply by 35% in 2030 and 141% in 2050.
source_name: Production Gap Report 2025

text: End fossil fuel subsidies. The IEA keeps flagging them as a perverse incentive that must be phased out, alongside a price on carbon.
source_name: IEEFA, on the IEA Net Zero by 2050 roadmap

text: Agree a shared exit roadmap. The idea did not make it into the COP30 deal, so a voluntary coalition led by Colombia and allied nations will carry it forward outside the UN process.
source_name: Dhaka Tribune, COP30 outcome

text: Clean power is winning, but not fast enough. In 2025 renewables overtook coal in the world's electricity mix for the first time in 100 years, at 33.8% against 33.0%.
source_name: Ember: Global Electricity Review 2026

text: Solar did most of the work. A record rise in solar power met 75% of the increase in global electricity demand in 2025.
source_name: Ember: Global Electricity Review 2026

text: The 2030 goal needs far more. The world added a record 693 GW of renewable capacity in 2025, but must average 1,200 GW a year from 2026 to 2030 to triple capacity.
source_name: Semafor, reporting IRENA's 2026 tracking report

text: Wires are the bottleneck. More than 2,500 GW of renewable, storage and large-demand projects are stalled in grid connection queues worldwide.
source_name: IEA: Electricity 2026 (grids)

text: Set national targets that add up to the global goal. At COP28, 133 countries agreed to triple installed renewable capacity by 2030 compared with 2022.
source_name: S&P Global, reporting IRENA's tracking

text: Build faster. IRENA says annual additions must almost double to about 1.2 TW over 2026-2030, with solar expected to be 42% of the 2030 total.
source_name: PV Tech, reporting IRENA

text: Clear the grid queues and build more grid. The IEA says annual grid investment must rise by about 50% from today's USD 400 billion by 2030.
source_name: IEA: Electricity 2026 (grids)

text: Add storage alongside. Tripling renewables means batteries growing about sixfold to 1,200 GW by 2030, to avoid grid bottlenecks.
source_name: E&E News, reporting the IEA

text: Make clean power replace fossil power, not just add to it. In 2025 it just did: low-carbon generation rose 887 TWh against 849 TWh of demand growth, so fossil generation fell slightly.
source_name: Ember: Global Electricity Review 2026

text: Carbon pricing is spreading but still covers under a third of emissions. Just over 29% of global greenhouse gas emissions face a direct carbon price, and the average price is nearly $21 a tonne.
source_name: World Bank: State and Trends of Carbon Pricing 2026

text: The price is far too low for the Paris goals. The IMF puts the global average price at about $5 a tonne, against about $85 a tonne by 2030 needed to be on track for 2 °C, and much more for 1.5 °C.
source_name: IMF Staff Climate Note 2024/006

text: Most priced emissions are priced lightly. In 2023 only about 16% of emissions faced an effective carbon rate above EUR 30 a tonne, and about 11% faced one above EUR 60.
source_name: OECD: Effective Carbon Rates 2025

text: Some trading systems are not true caps. By 2023, 12 of 34 emissions trading systems set their limit by output (intensity) rather than a fixed total, up from 2 of 20 in 2018.
source_name: OECD: Effective Carbon Rates 2025 (press release)

text: Set a price that rises toward what the science needs. The IMF says a global carbon price of $85 a tonne by 2030 would put emissions on track for 2 °C, with much more needed for 1.5 °C.
source_name: IMF Staff Climate Note 2024/006

text: Cap total emissions, not emissions per unit of output. China plans absolute caps from 2027 for sectors with stable emissions, and a system mixing free and auctioned allowances by 2030.
source_name: ICAP: China guidelines on absolute caps and wider scope

text: Cover more of the economy. China's national market now includes steel, cement and aluminium alongside power, and covers around 60% of the country's emissions.
source_name: Columbia Center on Global Energy Policy: China

text: Watch how free allowances are handed out. The OECD finds that linking free allowances to current output has become more common, even in cap-and-trade systems, so design choices shape how much of the price companies actually feel.
source_name: OECD: Effective Carbon Rates 2025 (press release)

text: Put the money to work. Governments raised a record $107 billion from carbon pricing in 2025, and the World Bank says it can fund development priorities and public budgets.
source_name: World Bank: State and Trends of Carbon Pricing 2026

text: Oil, gas and coal operations leak about 124 Mt of methane a year, around 35% of human-caused methane, and the IEA saw no sign of a fall in 2025.
source_name: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026 (as reported by Al Jazeera)

text: Around 70% of fossil fuel methane comes from the 10 highest-emitting countries, so a few governments decide most of the outcome.
source_name: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026

text: Average methane intensity of oil and gas production has fallen about 10% since 2019, but the best performers are over 100 times better than the worst.
source_name: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026

text: Policies in place today would cut oil and gas methane only about 20% by 2030, short of the Global Methane Pledge goal of a 30% cut.
source_name: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026

text: Cut human-caused methane by up to 45% (about 180 Mt a year) by 2030, which would avoid nearly 0.3 °C of warming by the 2040s.
source_name: UNEP and CCAC Global Methane Assessment 2021

text: Use the fossil fuel fixes that already exist: leak repair, ending venting and flaring, and coal mine gas capture. No new technology is needed.
source_name: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026

text: Sell the saved gas: abatement could make about 200 bcm of natural gas available each year.
source_name: IEA, Tackling methane emissions (May 2026)

text: Importers can set near-zero methane standards. The EU, China, UK, Japan and Korea doing so could cut upstream oil and gas methane about 20%.
source_name: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026

text: Turn pledges into rules: most Global Methane Pledge signatories have yet to adopt concrete policies to cut emissions.
source_name: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026

text: Farming is the biggest human source of methane, about 42% of the global total, mostly from livestock digestion, rice fields and manure.
source_name: Down To Earth (reporting UNEP/CCAC Global Methane Status Report 2025)

text: Roll out feed additives and better livestock breeding. UNEP counts about 24 million tonnes of farm methane that could be cut by 2030 with feed additives, breeding, rice water management and a ban on burning farm waste.
source_name: Down To Earth (reporting UNEP/CCAC Global Methane Status Report 2025)

text: Change how rice fields are watered. Practices that raise the oxygen level in paddy soil cut the methane the field produces.
source_name: FAO LEAP Partnership: Methane emissions in livestock and rice systems (2023)

text: Put farm methane into national plans with measurable targets. FAO found 85 Global Methane Pledge countries had added farm methane measures, but few say how much they will cut.
source_name: Clean Air Task Force (citing FAO analysis)

text: Steel and cement together cause about 14% of global energy and process-related emissions on a direct basis.
source_name: IEA, Steel and Cement Transition (2025)

text: Iron and steel alone is about 11% of global CO2 emissions; to fit the IEA 1.5 °C path its direct emissions must fall to 1.8 Gt by 2030.
source_name: World Economic Forum, citing IEA

text: China's heavy industry emissions are generally on a declining trend.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker, China

text: From 2000 to 2023, public finance for industrial decarbonisation in emerging and developing economies totalled only USD 1.5 bn.
source_name: OECD-IEA study (reported by Devdiscourse)

text: Invest nearly USD 400 bn in near-zero steel and cement in emerging economies in 2026-2035, out of a global need above USD 500 bn.
source_name: OECD-IEA study (reported by Devdiscourse)

text: Agree one definition of near-zero steel: the IEA threshold is 400 to 50 kg CO2e per tonne of crude steel, depending on scrap share.
source_name: IEA, Near-zero steel and cement definitions (2024)

text: Price industrial carbon: China's national ETS added cement, steel and aluminium in 2025 and plans to cover all major emissions-intensive industries by 2027.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker, China

text: Create demand for clean materials, including rules that require a growing market share of near-zero emissions materials.
source_name: IEA, Steel and Cement Transition (2025)

text: Fund the shift: COP29's pledge for international help with industry decarbonisation committed USD 1.3 bn.
source_name: IEA, Breakthrough Agenda Report 2025 (steel)

text: If fully delivered, current national climate plans (NDCs) cut emissions only 5-8% by 2030 and 11-15% by 2035, versus 2025 levels.
source_name: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026

text: By 1 September 2026, 124 Paris Agreement parties covering about 76% of global emissions had submitted new NDCs.
source_name: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 (reported by Eco-Business)

text: If all NDCs are delivered and similar efforts continue, warming would be limited to 2.6 °C.
source_name: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026

text: Net-zero targets covering around 80% of global emissions still lack legal backing.
source_name: OECD Climate Action Monitor 2026

text: Cut global emissions 18% by 2030 and 45% by 2035 versus 2025 to follow the lowest-overshoot path.
source_name: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026

text: Average a 5.7% fall in emissions every year from 2025 to 2035.
source_name: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 (reported by Eco-Business)

text: Close the 2035 gap of 16 GtCO2e, which widens to 22 GtCO2e under current policies.
source_name: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 (reported by Eco-Business)

text: Put net-zero targets into law so they last.
source_name: OECD Climate Action Monitor 2026

text: Line up near-term targets with long-term national goals, which are not yet fully aligned.
source_name: OECD Climate Action Monitor 2026

text: Electric car sales passed 20 million in 2025, one quarter of all new cars sold.
source_name: IEA Global EV Outlook 2026

text: Electric cars are now expected to reach 29% of world car sales in 2026.
source_name: IEA, Electric Car Markets in a Time of Uncertainty

text: About 5% of the global car stock is electrified, displacing 1.2 million barrels of oil a day in 2025.
source_name: IEA Global EV Outlook 2026

text: US electric car share is only about 10%, and the IEA expects virtually no government purchase support there in 2026.
source_name: IEA Global EV Outlook 2026 (reported by Rest of World)

text: Raise the electric share of car sales everywhere: China is set for almost 60% in 2026, the EU reached just under 27% in 2025.
source_name: IEA Global EV Outlook 2026

text: Electrify trucks, helped by emissions standards such as the EU's and by falling costs, especially in China.
source_name: IEA Global EV Outlook 2026

text: Keep purchase support steady: Canada's electric share fell from nearly 17% to 11% after a rebate ended.
source_name: IEA Global EV Outlook 2026 (reported by Rest of World)

text: Set clear non-fossil energy targets: China's 15th Five-Year Plan sets 25% by 2030 and 30% by 2035.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker, China

text: Use the oil-price shock: more than 90 countries grew electric car sales in the first half of 2026.
source_name: IEA, Electric Car Markets in a Time of Uncertainty

text: World energy investment is set to reach USD 3.4 trillion in 2026, with about USD 2.2 trillion going to clean energy.
source_name: IEA World Energy Investment 2026 (reported by ThisDay)

text: In 2025, 85% of energy projects in advanced economies used commercial finance, against 67% in emerging and developing economies.
source_name: IEA World Energy Investment 2026

text: International public adaptation finance to developing countries was USD 28.2-31.7 bn in 2024, up only USD 1 bn on 2023.
source_name: UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2026

text: Adaptation needs are estimated at USD 305 bn a year by 2035.
source_name: UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2026

text: Triple adaptation finance by 2035, as the COP30 aspiration says, while knowing that would cover only 20-29% of needs.
source_name: UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2026

text: Put least developed countries and small island states first: tripling flows to them could meet 49-84% of their needs.
source_name: UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2026

text: Cut the cost of capital in emerging economies, where borrowing costs are significantly higher than in advanced economies.
source_name: IEA World Energy Investment 2026 (reported by ThisDay)

text: Bring in much more private finance, because needs go beyond what public money alone can cover.
source_name: IEA and IFC (via World Economic Forum)

text: Fund loss and damage: the first round of requests to the fund came to USD 2.8 bn, far above its initial funding.
source_name: UNEP Adaptation Gap Report 2026

text: National net-zero commitments still cover 77% of global GDP; with US state targets included, coverage is 83%.
source_name: Net Zero Tracker (via EurekAlert)

text: Many countries risk missing national targets that are now only a few years away unless implementation speeds up.
source_name: OECD Climate Action Monitor 2026

text: 860 of the 1,245 Forbes Global 2000 companies with net-zero targets back them with plans.
source_name: Net Zero Tracker (via EurekAlert)

text: China's 15th Five-Year Plan sets a 17% carbon-intensity cut for 2030, lowered from 18% after the earlier goal was missed.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker, China

text: Turn targets into implementation plans with named actions and owners.
source_name: OECD Climate Action Monitor 2026

text: Include credible parts in every target: interim goals and robust plans.
source_name: NewClimate Institute, Net Zero Stocktake 2025

text: Keep residual emissions in net-zero target years small; they can reach up to a fifth of current emissions.
source_name: Climate Action Tracker, net zero evaluations

text: Use state and city action: 19 US states remain committed to net zero.
source_name: Net Zero Tracker (via EurekAlert)

text: Align near-term targets with long-term goals, which are not yet fully aligned.
source_name: OECD Climate Action Monitor 2026

text: Global deforestation fell 15% in 2025 to seven million hectares, but the world is off track to halt it by 2030.
source_name: Forest Declaration Assessment 2026 (reported by Down To Earth)

text: The tropics lost 4.3 million hectares of primary forest in 2025, down 36% on 2024 but 46% above a decade ago.
source_name: WRI Global Forest Watch

text: Fires accounted for 42% of tropical forest destruction in 2025.
source_name: WRI and University of Maryland (reported by Al Jazeera)

text: Protected areas cover 17.33% of the world's land and inland waters, against a 30% target for 2030.
source_name: Forest Declaration Assessment 2026 (reported by Down To Earth)

text: Enforce forest laws: Brazil cut non-fire primary forest loss 41% in 2025, its lowest on record.
source_name: WRI Global Forest Watch

text: Cut deforestation about 10% a year against the 2018-2020 baseline to end it by 2030.
source_name: WRI Forest Pledges Tracker

text: Tackle the main driver: farmland expansion converts primary forest to pasture and plantations.
source_name: Forest Declaration Assessment (via Climate Home News)

text: Expand protected areas from 17.33% towards the 30% target.
source_name: Forest Declaration Assessment 2026 (reported by Down To Earth)

text: Recognise Indigenous land rights, which many communities still lack in law.
source_name: Forest Declaration Assessment 2026 (reported by Down To Earth)

text: Russia and the United States hold 79% of the world's weapons-usable nuclear material, so their security practices matter most.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026: executive summary

text: Stockpiles of plutonium are growing in several countries, including France, India and Russia.
source_name: NTI: 2026 Nuclear Security Index findings

text: Russia's score fell mainly because it suspended international cooperation and produced more weapons-usable material.
source_name: NTI: 2026 Nuclear Security Index news release

text: Actively reduce the total stockpile of weapons-usable nuclear material, and stop running enrichment plants that handle highly enriched uranium.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Publish regular public reports on civilian and military stocks of weapons-usable material.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Minimise stocks and the number of sites that hold them, and eliminate them where possible.
source_name: NTI: nuclear security priorities

text: The two biggest holders, Russia and the United States, reverse their security declines first.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026: take action

text: The rise in plutonium stocks is largely driven by spent fuel reprocessing, which quickly builds up weapons-usable material and creates unnecessary security risks.
source_name: NTI: 2026 Nuclear Security Index news release

text: Russia scores 0 out of 100 on quantities and sites, down 20 points, because its material stocks are increasing.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026: Russia profile

text: Commit to forgoing reprocessing of nuclear fuel, and act on that commitment.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Operate no reprocessing plants that handle highly enriched uranium or separated plutonium.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Fully license at least one site for permanent, irretrievable storage of spent fuel.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Of the 50 countries and areas with weapons-usable material or nuclear facilities, only 26 require employees at nuclear facilities to report suspicious activity.
source_name: NTI: 5 data points from the 2026 NTI Index

text: Only 12 of those 50 require annual cybersecurity assessments at the sites that host the material.
source_name: NTI: 5 data points from the 2026 NTI Index

text: Vet security staff and others with access to nuclear material areas at least every two years.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Set up rules for staff to report suspicious behaviour, and require insider-threat training for all personnel.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Require extra training or certification for personnel with security duties.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: The United States scores 33 out of 100 on security culture, down 34 points since 2023, its biggest drop.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026: United States profile

text: Have an independent regulator with its own authority, budget and legal powers.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Mandate annual nuclear security culture self-assessments.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Require a regularly updated Design Basis Threat, the threat that security must be built to withstand.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Require regular tests of security systems, including realistic force-on-force exercises.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: The next milestone is the 2027 Review Conference of the Amended Convention on the Physical Protection of Nuclear Material (CPPNM).
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026: India profile

text: Ratify the International Convention for the Suppression of Acts of Nuclear Terrorism.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Ratify Additional Protocol I to the Geneva Conventions, which prohibits attacks on nuclear facilities.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Endorse and follow the IAEA's Seven Indispensable Pillars for nuclear safety and security during armed conflict.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: Complete the national legal framework for the Amended CPPNM and join the Global Forum to Prevent Radiological and Nuclear Terrorism.
source_name: NTI Nuclear Security Index 2026, country profiles

text: States are increasingly relying on nuclear weapons as instruments of national power, even as the risks of miscalculation and escalation rise.
source_name: SIPRI Yearbook 2026: press release

text: The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists set the Doomsday Clock at 85 seconds to midnight in January 2026, the closest it has been.
source_name: Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists: Doomsday Clock

text: Risk reduction means information exchanges, operating limits and transparency steps that are less formal than arms control, such as crisis hotlines and missile launch notifications.
source_name: Congressional Research Service: Nuclear Risk Reduction (IN12717)

text: India and Pakistan exchange lists of their nuclear installations every 1 January under a 1988 agreement not to attack them. The 35th exchange took place on 1 January 2026, despite the May 2025 conflict.
source_name: All India Radio News (1 Jan 2026)

text: North Korea stopped answering the twice-daily calls on the inter-Korean military hotline in October 2026; an analyst quoted by AFP said the lack of hotlines raises the risk of unintended escalation.
source_name: AFP via Cambodianess (Oct 2026)

text: In January 2026 Israel and Iran exchanged pledges not to strike first, passed through Russia rather than directly, according to diplomats cited by The Washington Post.
source_name: The Washington Post via The Philadelphia Inquirer (14 Jan 2026)

text: An Israel Hayom analysis notes there is no direct communication channel between Israel and Iran, so each round of tension carries a higher risk of escalation by miscalculation.
source_name: Israel Hayom (21 Dec 2025)

text: Keep reliable crisis hotlines and military-to-military contacts open, and give advance notice of major exercises.
source_name: European Leadership Network: Beyond the Rome Declaration

text: Take weapons off high alert (de-alerting) so leaders have more time to decide before any launch.
source_name: European Leadership Network: Beyond the Rome Declaration

text: Commit never to use nuclear weapons first, and give advance notice of military activity.
source_name: ICRC working paper for the 2026 NPT Review Conference

text: Agree ballistic missile launch notifications and nuclear crisis communication among the five nuclear-weapon states.
source_name: Congressional Research Service: Nuclear Risk Reduction (IN12717)

text: New START, the last US-Russia limit on strategic nuclear weapons, expired in February 2026 with no replacement.
source_name: SIPRI Yearbook 2026: world nuclear forces

text: Russia and the United States together hold about 83% of all stockpiled warheads.
source_name: SIPRI Yearbook 2026: press release

text: No new trilateral talks involving China, Russia and the United States are under way.
source_name: Brussels Signal (reporting SIPRI Yearbook 2026)

text: Open talks on a successor to New START. The Hiroshima Report found no progress on one.
source_name: Hiroshima Report 2026: executive summary

text: Restore the data sharing that New START provided. Russia and the United States no longer publish aggregate strategic force numbers.
source_name: SIPRI Yearbook 2026 (chart notes)

text: Bring China into arms control talks alongside Russia and the United States.
source_name: Brussels Signal (reporting SIPRI Yearbook 2026)

text: Advance no-first-use commitments, which would let militaries plan for smaller arsenals and de-alerting.
source_name: Pugwash: working group recommendations

text: The Yale/Columbia index scores how much of each of 14 land habitat types sits inside protected areas or other effective conservation measures. Protecting 30% of every habitat type scores 100.
source_name: Yale/Columbia Environmental Performance Index 2026: Terrestrial Biome Protection

text: Under the Global Biodiversity Framework, governments agreed to conserve at least 30% of land, inland waters, coasts and seas by 2030, in systems that are representative, well connected and fairly governed.
source_name: CBD: Global Biodiversity Framework targets with guidance notes

text: Count and map land that is already conserved but not yet reported, including land managed by Indigenous peoples and local communities, which could cover more than 35% of the world's land.
source_name: Campaign for Nature, 30x30 Global Assessment 2026 (Devdiscourse report)

text: Aim new protection at habitats that are under-covered, not only the easiest land. A study of 25 countries found extra conserved land that does not substantially close the gaps in ecological representativeness.
source_name: O'Neill et al., Nature: Global conservation area coverage substantially exceeds current estimates

text: Fund and staff the sites that already exist. Scientists warn that expanding coverage alone has not halted nature loss, and that much funding goes to new sites over existing ones.
source_name: Down To Earth: Protected areas expanding fast but failing to halt nature loss

text: The Species Habitat Index measures how much of the suitable habitat for a country's species is still intact compared with 2001. A score of 100 means no habitat loss since 2001.
source_name: Yale/Columbia Environmental Performance Index 2026: Species Habitat Index

text: The Biodiversity Habitat Index estimates how habitat loss, degradation and fragmentation affect how much land biodiversity is expected to keep. A score of 100 means little loss or degradation.
source_name: Yale/Columbia Environmental Performance Index 2026: Biodiversity Habitat Index

text: Plan land and sea use for nature, so the loss of areas of high biodiversity importance is brought close to zero by 2030 (Global Biodiversity Framework Target 1).
source_name: CBD: Global Biodiversity Framework targets with guidance notes

text: Tackle the biggest direct driver of species decline, which the UN-backed IPBES assessment ranked first: land conversion, including deforestation for farming.
source_name: National Geographic, reporting the IPBES Global Assessment

text: The Red List Index tracks the average extinction risk of a country's species, weighting each species by how much of its range falls inside the country. A score of 100 means none of the assessed species is threatened.
source_name: Yale/Columbia Environmental Performance Index 2026: Red List Index

text: The IPBES global assessment found around 1 million animal and plant species threatened with extinction, many within decades.
source_name: United Nations, IPBES Global Assessment press release, 2019

text: Halt human-caused extinction of known threatened species, and recover and conserve species so their populations are healthy and resilient (Global Biodiversity Framework Target 4).
source_name: CBD: Global Biodiversity Framework targets with guidance notes

text: Act on the drivers the IPBES assessment named: land conversion, overfishing, hunting and poaching, climate change, pollution and invasive alien species.
source_name: National Geographic, reporting the IPBES Global Assessment

text: The Bioclimatic Ecosystem Resilience Index estimates how well natural ecosystems can keep their variety of species as the climate changes. It is based on ecosystem area, connectivity and integrity.
source_name: Yale/Columbia Environmental Performance Index 2026: Bioclimatic Ecosystem Resilience Index

text: Restore at least 30% of degraded land, inland water, coastal and marine ecosystems by 2030 (Global Biodiversity Framework Target 2).
source_name: CBD: Global Biodiversity Framework targets with guidance notes

text: Keep protected and conserved areas joined up. Target 3 calls for systems that are well connected, so species can move as conditions change.
source_name: CBD: Global Biodiversity Framework targets with guidance notes

text: Governments pay out money that ends up harming nature. The Global Biodiversity Framework says to cut harmful incentives by at least $500 billion a year by 2030, and to scale up incentives that help nature.
source_name: CBD: Global Biodiversity Framework targets with guidance notes

text: The UN's 2026 progress report found far fewer countries have committed to reducing harmful subsidies than to promoting positive incentives.
source_name: Bernama-Xinhua, reporting the CBD State of Biodiversity Action report, 15 Oct 2026

text: Identify the incentives and subsidies that harm biodiversity, then phase them out or reform them (Global Biodiversity Framework Target 18).
source_name: CBD: Global Biodiversity Framework targets with guidance notes

text: Scale up positive incentives for conserving and using nature sustainably, and move investment toward nature-positive activity, as the UN Secretary-General urged at the report launch.
source_name: Bernama-Xinhua, reporting the CBD State of Biodiversity Action report, 15 Oct 2026

text: The Global Hunger Index counts undernourishment, the share of people who do not get enough food energy, as one third of each country's score.
source_name: 2026 Global Hunger Index, methodology (Welthungerhilfe, Concern, Helvetas, IFHV)

text: About 645 million people faced hunger in 2025, 7.8% of the world, down from 8.1% in 2024. A third of the world still cannot afford a healthy diet.
source_name: FAO, State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026 (press release)

text: Get cash and social protection to hungry households. A review of sub-Saharan Africa finds cash transfers, the widest-reaching social protection scheme, work best for food security over time when paired with other economic and social support.
source_name: Burchi, Scarlato and d'Agostino, Poverty & Public Policy, 2018

text: Bring down the cost of a healthy diet. The 2026 UN report says food value chains are a major determinant of prices, and that animal-source foods are the largest cost in Africa.
source_name: UNICEF, State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026 (press release)

text: Prevent and reduce the effect of conflict on hunger, and hold to account those who use hunger as a weapon of war. The index calls conflict the primary driver of global hunger.
source_name: Global Hunger Index, policy recommendations

text: Child stunting is the share of children under five who are too short for their age. It reflects chronic undernutrition and counts for one sixth of the score.
source_name: 2026 Global Hunger Index, methodology

text: Stunting among children under five fell from 26.4% (180.4 million) in 2012 to 23.2% (150.2 million) in 2024. That is not fast enough to reach the 2030 target of 16.8%.
source_name: UNICEF Data, State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026

text: Keep the focus on the first 1,000 days. The 2021 Lancet series found stunting and wasting peak in the first six months of life and exist in part at birth.
source_name: Devex, reporting the Lancet series on maternal and child undernutrition, 2021

text: Scale up the proven nutrition package. A 129-country model found scaling 18 interventions to 95% coverage raises the countries on track for the stunting target from 46 to 50, so more than nutrition programmes is needed.
source_name: Scott et al., BMC Medicine, 2020

text: Close the delivery and funding gap. The 2021 Lancet series says delivery has lagged behind the science and more financing is needed to scale up proven interventions.
source_name: Lancet series on maternal and child undernutrition, 2021 (Medical Xpress summary)

text: Child wasting is the share of children under five who are too thin for their height. It reflects acute undernutrition and counts for one sixth of the score.
source_name: 2026 Global Hunger Index, methodology

text: 42.8 million children are affected by wasting, 12.2 million of them severely, the deadliest form.
source_name: UNICEF, 30 years of therapeutic food (press release, 5 May 2026)

text: Treat severe wasting in the community with ready-to-use therapeutic food. UNICEF reports a recovery rate of nearly 90% for children treated for severe acute malnutrition.
source_name: UNICEF, 30 years of therapeutic food (press release, 5 May 2026)

text: Keep the supply of therapeutic food and milk steady. UNICEF says the full range of treatment must be scaled up so it can withstand supply shocks, reduce costs and reach every child who needs it.
source_name: UNICEF, 30 years of therapeutic food (press release, 5 May 2026)

text: The index gives child mortality, the share of children who die before age five, one third of the score. That is the same weight as undernourishment.
source_name: 2026 Global Hunger Index, Our World in Data

text: Stunting, wasting and micronutrient deficiencies are estimated to underlie nearly 3.1 million child deaths a year, according to the 2013 Lancet nutrition series.
source_name: Bhutta et al., The Lancet, 2013 maternal and child nutrition series

text: Find and treat children who are both stunted and wasted. The 2021 Lancet series found 4.7% of children have both, a condition linked to 4.8 times the risk of death.
source_name: Lancet series on maternal and child undernutrition, 2021 (Medical Xpress summary)

text: Deliver the long-standing interventions with the strongest evidence, such as breastfeeding promotion and vitamin A supplementation.
source_name: Devex, reporting the Lancet series on maternal and child undernutrition, 2021

text: Keep up breastfeeding gains. The share of infants under six months who are exclusively breastfed rose from 37.0% in 2012 to 47.4%.
source_name: UNICEF Data, State of Food Security and Nutrition in the World 2026

text: The 2026 Global Report on Food Crises had the lowest country coverage in its ten-year history. 18 countries and territories lacked data that met its requirements, including Burkina Faso, the Republic of the Congo and Ethiopia.
source_name: Down To Earth, reporting the Global Report on Food Crises 2026

text: The 2026 index warns that funding cuts weaken monitoring, so emergencies can go unnoticed once data on undernourishment and child mortality stop being collected.
source_name: The Wire, reporting the 2026 Global Hunger Index

text: Fund the data systems behind hunger assessments. The 2026 food-crises report warns their integrity is increasingly at risk as money falls, and calls for funding, monitoring and responding.
source_name: Down To Earth, reporting the Global Report on Food Crises 2026

text: Act earlier, and protect local food systems instead of relying only on food assistance. The head of IFAD said the response must move from reacting too late to acting early.
source_name: IFAD, Global Report on Food Crises 2026 (press release, 24 Apr 2026)

text: Zero-dose children are children who have not had any routine vaccine. In practice they are counted as children who did not get a first DTP dose.
source_name: Gavi, programme funding guidelines (zero-dose definition)

text: About 13.5 million children got no vaccine in their first year in 2025, nearly 750,000 fewer than the year before. More than half live in fragile or conflict-affected settings.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: The Immunization Agenda 2030 aims to halve the number of zero-dose children from the 2019 level by 2030. The 2025 count was 3.9 million above the milestone for that year.
source_name: WHO and UNICEF, WUENIC 2025: progress and challenges

text: Use the Identify, Reach, Monitor, Measure, Advocate approach that Gavi funds: find where zero-dose children live, design ways to reach them, track progress and press for support.
source_name: Gavi, programme funding guidelines (IRMMA framework)

text: Strengthen immunization in conflict and fragile settings so children are reached and kept in care.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: Third-dose DTP coverage is used as the marker of how well a country delivers routine immunization. Global coverage was 85% in 2025.
source_name: UNICEF Data, Vaccination and immunization statistics

text: In 2025, 7.3 million infants got a first DTP dose but did not go on to get a first measles dose.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: Remind families when a dose is due or missed. A Cochrane review found reminders likely raise vaccination by about 8 percentage points on average, and phone reminders worked best.
source_name: Cochrane review CD003941, reminder and recall for immunization

text: Check immunization data against other sources and run targeted surveys to find where children are missed and why.
source_name: Gavi Zero-Dose Learning Hub, national toolkit (2026)

text: First-dose measles coverage was 84% worldwide in 2025 and second-dose coverage 77%. Both are well short of the 95% needed to prevent outbreaks.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: Measles vaccination saved nearly 59 million lives between 2000 and 2024, and measles deaths fell 88% over that time.
source_name: WHO, measles deaths down 88% since 2000 (28 Nov 2025)

text: Counter false and misleading health information and support efforts to speed up vaccine uptake.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: Catch up children who missed doses. WHO, UNICEF and Gavi called for continued investment in the Big Catch-Up launched in 2023.
source_name: WHO, UNICEF and Gavi, World Immunization Week release (24 Apr 2025)

text: A second measles dose, usually given at 15 to 18 months, protects children whose first dose did not make them immune.
source_name: Masresha et al., Vaccines, 2024

text: By the end of 2023, 43 of 47 countries in the WHO African Region had added the second measles dose to their routine schedule.
source_name: Masresha et al., Vaccines, 2024

text: Add the second dose to the national schedule. Since 2017 WHO has recommended this for every country, whatever its first-dose coverage.
source_name: Masresha et al., lessons from second-dose introduction in Africa, 2018

text: Give the second measles dose alongside other vaccines in the second year of life. Countries that give more vaccines at that age had higher second-dose coverage and fewer drop-outs.
source_name: Masresha et al., Vaccines, 2024

text: Only 18 national immunization surveys were submitted for the 2025 estimates, down from 50 in 2024 and an average of 33 a year in 2015 to 2019.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: WHO and UNICEF say the full impact of the health aid cuts announced over the past two years is not yet reflected in the estimates.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: Increase and sustain domestic and global funding for immunization programmes and partnerships, including Gavi.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: Invest in stronger data and disease surveillance systems to guide immunization programmes.
source_name: UNICEF and WHO, 2025 immunization coverage estimates (press release, 15 Jul 2026)

text: Gavi's 2026 to 2030 strategy is not yet fully funded, so countries face hard choices about which immunization programmes to prioritise.
source_name: Gavi, 2025 coverage estimates release (15 Jul 2026)

text: 55 countries (41%) have frameworks on children's rights in AI, and only 27 show evidence of putting them into practice.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Of 55 countries with gender-related AI frameworks, 24 show evidence of implementation.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: 47 countries (35%) have frameworks on cultural and linguistic diversity, and few require developers to use diverse datasets.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Write gender equality, children's rights and cultural and linguistic diversity into AI frameworks, and show they are being carried out.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Go beyond funding local-language AI: require developers to build for local languages and use diverse datasets.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Transparency and explainability is the strongest indicator in the index: 58% of countries have some framework for it.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Only 27% of countries have frameworks on AI's environmental effects, and 83% of those are non-binding.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Require disclosure of AI's energy use, water use and environmental impact, which very few governments do today.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Make fairness, transparency and human-oversight rules binding, not voluntary.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: 39 countries (29%) have labour protection frameworks for AI, against 72 (53%) with reskilling and upskilling frameworks.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: AI literacy is one of the strongest indicators: 71 countries (53%) have a framework.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Add protections for workers affected by AI, including their rights to organise and bargain collectively, alongside skills programmes.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: GIRAI found credible evidence of government misuse of AI in 35 of 135 countries.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Only 36% of countries have frameworks on AI-facilitated misinformation and violence.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Set up independent oversight bodies and audits, and give people affected by AI a way to seek redress.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 priorities

text: Cover AI-driven misinformation and violence in law. Only 36% of countries have frameworks for it.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: AI Use in Public Service is the weakest dimension: frameworks cover its indicators in 31% of cases, against a 42% average.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Only 18% of countries require disclosure of the AI systems government uses, and 26% have frameworks for buying AI fairly and accountably.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Publish the algorithmic systems government uses, so people can see where AI affects decisions about them.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Set procurement rules for AI, as Brazil, Chile and Australia have, including guards against vendor lock-in.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings

text: Give civil society a formal role in AI policy. Only 36 countries (27%) have working mechanisms for it.
source_name: Global Center on AI Governance, GIRAI 2026 key findings
